top_categories.workout_context: 320 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Styrkeprøven's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
13,845ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 320 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Road-specific control matters at Styrkeprøven. Practice on paved Norwegian roads from Trondheim across: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 320 miles.
Styrkeprøven's paved Norwegian roads from Trondheim across rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
320 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 13,845ft of climbing on paved Norwegian roads from Trondheim across does to your power file on race day.
At Styrkeprøven, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
13,845ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Styrkeprøven. Train it until it feels boring.
Tempo is Styrkeprøven's race pace. The wattage you'll hold for 320 miles on paved Norwegian roads from Trondheim across. Train it until it's automatic.

race_overlay.weather: June in Trondheim to Oslo, Norway — Late June near the summer solstice means near-continuous daylight: sunrise around 3:00 AM, sunset past 10:40 PM. The route crosses Dovrefjell, a mountain plateau at 1,000+ meters where snow has been recorded in June and temperatures can hover near freezing even in midsummer. The first 120 km climb from sea level to the plateau brings dramatic temperature drops. The midsummer night never truly darkens, creating an ethereal riding atmosphere through the small hours. Wind on the exposed plateau regularly reaches 15 m/s. Rain and fog are common. Riders must be prepared for conditions spanning 5-20C (41-68F) in a single ride. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Styrkeprøven. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 320 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 320 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Styrkeprøven. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and VO2max to prepare you for 320 miles of paved norwegian roads from trondheim across dovrefjell mountain plateau to oslo in Trondheim to Oslo, Norway.
